title: Hold the non-RTL required contexts (docs.yml, elaborate.yml) in the ci_events perimeter
body:
## Problem

The ci_events gate holds the run/no-run perimeter of both RTL workflows, but the four non-RTL required contexts sit outside it. Measured at `70421f5c` (and equally at `dev@a8b27a5f`, so this predates PR #239), each of these mutants returns `checked=171 findings=0`:

- `if: false` on the `docs-check` job in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
- `continue-on-error: true` on the `elaborate` job in `.github/workflows/elaborate.yml`

`check_docs` holds only triggers and the ci_events wiring text; `check_elaborate` only triggers and the one-carrier name; neither runs `check_job_keys`, and `PUBLIC_NAMES` in `scripts/ci_events.py` omits `docs-check`, `docs-check-no-git` and `wire-accountability`, so the one-carrier rule does not cover them either.

Impact: `if: false` on `docs-check` retires the ci_events gate itself (docs.yml is the only workflow that runs `--check`/`--selftest`) while every required context stays satisfied, because a skipped required context satisfies the ruleset. The same lever on `elaborate` retires the elaboration gate.

Found by the round-6 review of PR #239 (recorded there as MINOR, out of that PR's scope: the hole predates the branch and sits outside issue #209's acceptance rows).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every job carrying a required check-run name in `docs.yml` and `elaborate.yml` has its neuter keys held by `scripts/ci_events.py --check` (no undocumented `if`, no `continue-on-error`, no `defaults`), the way the RTL workflows' jobs are held.
2. `docs-check`, `docs-check-no-git` and `wire-accountability` join the one-carrier (exactly one job per public name) rule.
3. The two mutants above, plus a `defaults` variant, are refused by `--check` naming the job, with reason-pinned non-vacuous selftest arms.
4. The pristine tree stays green, and `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` states the widened perimeter.
